claims.text: The material under study is equimolar WTaTiVZr.
WTaTiVZr has superior plastic strain to commercially pure tungsten under high-temperature plasma-facing conditions.
WTaTiVZr has superior toughness to commercially pure tungsten under high-temperature plasma-facing conditions.
The proposed superiority in plastic strain and toughness is governed by lattice distortion in the multicomponent solid solution.
Lattice distortion promotes activation of additional slip systems.
Lattice distortion enhances dislocation mobility.
Enhanced slip-system activation and dislocation mobility lower the effective ductile-to-brittle transition.
Size mismatch among W, Ta, Ti, V, and Zr produces atomic lattice distortion and local stress fields.
The local stress fields generated by lattice distortion facilitate dislocation nucleation.
Lattice distortion in WTaTiVZr reduces stacking-fault energy.
Lattice distortion in WTaTiVZr lowers barriers to dislocation motion.
Pure tungsten has a more uniform lattice and a higher ductile-to-brittle transition temperature than WTaTiVZr.
Under identical high-temperature plasma-facing conditions, WTaTiVZr will have lower yield strength than pure tungsten.
Under identical high-temperature plasma-facing conditions, WTaTiVZr will sustain greater plastic strain before failure than pure tungsten.
Under identical high-temperature plasma-facing conditions, WTaTiVZr will have higher fracture toughness than pure tungsten.
Deformed WTaTiVZr will exhibit more distributed dislocation activity and evidence of more activated slip systems than pure tungsten.
Temperatures at or above 1000 K and high-energy flux are representative of plasma-facing-component service relevant to this hypothesis.
At lower temperatures, insufficient thermal activation will reduce the proposed ductility benefit of lattice distortion.
Processing history and irradiation-induced defects may alter the magnitude of the toughness and slip-activation effects.
Matching grain size and minimizing secondary phases in WTaTiVZr and pure tungsten is intended to control microstructural confounders.
